enzyme_name: beta-alanine N-methyltransferase (SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase of beta-alanine betaine synthesis)
organism_context: Limonium latifolium and other Plumbaginaceae
rationale: A single 43-kDa polypeptide (native homodimer) purified 1890-fold from Limonium latifolium carries out all three successive SAM-dependent N-methylations of beta-alanine, including the N-methyl -> N,N-dimethyl step written here. The source paper calls it 'trifunctional', but all three are the same N-methylation chemistry on one acceptor series at one active site, not distinct catalytic activities.
direction_note: Methyl transfer from SAM to an amine is physiologically unidirectional (SAH is scavenged), so the methylating left-to-right direction is the enzymatic one and ModelSEED's reverse-only call inverts it.

enzyme_name: benzoic acid carboxyl methyltransferase (BAMT; benzoate/salicylate carboxyl methyltransferase BSMT, SABATH family)
organism_context: Antirrhinum majus (snapdragon) floral BAMT; BSMT orthologues in Petunia, Clarkia, Arabidopsis
rationale: BAMT purified from snapdragon flowers is a homodimeric SABATH carboxyl methyltransferase with one catalytic activity, SAM-dependent methyl-esterification of benzoate. BSMT relatives also accept salicylate, but that is broad substrate specificity at a single active site, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Ester formation from SAM is the only reaction the enzyme performs and methyl benzoate is lost by volatilisation, so there is no physiological reverse flux; ModelSEED's reverse-only direction is backwards.

enzyme_name: sarcosine reductase (selenoprotein A + sarcosine-binding protein B + acetyl-phosphate-forming protein C)
organism_context: Tissierella creatinophila, Eubacterium acidaminophilum, Clostridium spp. (Stickland reduction of sarcosine)
rationale: Sarcosine reductase is a multi-protein selenoenzyme system - 21-kDa selenoprotein A, the sarcosine-specific substrate-binding protein B, and the two-subunit (62 + 50 kDa) acetyl-phosphate-forming protein C - i.e. an associating complex, not a fused bifunctional chain, so the subunit running this reductive C-N cleavage counts as monofunctional under the complex rule.
direction_note: The two-electron donor (thioredoxin / selenoprotein A couple) is absent and three bare protons stand in for the reducing equivalents (ModelSEED flags CI:-2); as an electron-accepting Stickland reaction it runs one way, sarcosine to methylamine + acetyl phosphate.

enzyme_name: p-coumaroyltriacetic acid synthase (CTAS / HmS, type III PKS); the isolated lactonisation step has no identified catalyst
organism_context: Hydrangea macrophylla var. thunbergii
rationale: CTAS (HmS) performs only the three decarboxylative condensations without cyclisation and releases a linear tetraketide that lactonises to the alpha-pyrone; no separate protein has been shown to catalyse the lactonisation that this MetaCyc entry isolates, so the catalyst for this specific step is undetermined.
direction_note: Intramolecular lactonisation of the released tetraketide is a spontaneous, effectively irreversible dehydration, so flux runs left to right as the council called it.

enzyme_name: catalase HPII / hydroperoxidase II (KatE) - autocatalytic protoheme IX to cis-heme d self-modification
organism_context: Escherichia coli; clade-3 large-subunit monofunctional catalase (contrast catalase-peroxidases KatG)
rationale: Loewen et al. showed HPII itself converts its own bound protoheme to cis-heme d by cis-hydroxylation using H2O2 as substrate, with distal His128 absolutely required. HPII is a monofunctional catalase - it has no second (peroxidatic) catalytic domain, unlike the bifunctional catalase-peroxidases.
direction_note: This is one-way oxidative self-processing driven by H2O2 consumption; wild-type heme d is not reconverted to heme b, so ModelSEED's reverse-only direction is physically impossible.

enzyme_name: 2-oxoadipate dehydrogenase complex (DHTKD1/E1a + DLST/E2 + DLD/E3) followed by glutaryl-CoA thioester cleavage
organism_context: mammalian L-lysine catabolism (DHTKD1); equivalent 2-oxoadipate route in Pseudomonas putida
rationale: No single enzyme turns 2-oxoadipate into glutarate: the committed step is NAD+/CoA-dependent oxidative decarboxylation to glutaryl-CoA by the 2-oxoadipate dehydrogenase complex, whose E1a subunit (DHTKD1) runs this chemistry and is monofunctional; the complex merely shares separate E2/E3 polypeptides with OGDH, which is not fused bifunctionality.
direction_note: At least two enzymes and the lost CO2 are collapsed into one entry (ModelSEED flags MI:C:-1/O:-1); the real oxidative decarboxylation is strongly exergonic and catabolically irreversible, i.e. left to right.

enzyme_name: ajmalan-type N-methyltransferase (norajmaline / acetylnorajmaline N-methyltransferase, gamma-tocopherol-like MT family)
organism_context: Rauvolfia serpentina roots (Apocynaceae)
rationale: N-methylation of the ajmalan indole nitrogen is performed by SAM-dependent NMTs of the gamma-tocopherol-like methyltransferase family, which show strict regiospecific single-activity N-methylation of ajmalan backbones; whether the two characterised enzymes accept the 17-O-acetylated substrate of this particular MetaCyc entry was not confirmed, so the enzyme identity is inferred.
direction_note: SAM and SAH are omitted - ModelSEED flags MI:C:1/H:2, exactly the missing methyl group - and with the methyl donor restored the methylation is irreversible left to right.

enzyme_name: flavonol 3-O-glucoside 2''-O-glucosyltransferase (UDP-glucose:flavonol-3-O-glucoside (1->2) glucosyltransferase, EC 2.4.1.239; family-1 UGT)
organism_context: Glycine max Fg3; Crocus sativus sophoroside-forming UGT; Arabidopsis flavonol glycoside pathway (AraCyc entry)
rationale: The enzymes that add the second glucose in (1->2) linkage onto a flavonol 3-O-glucoside are single-domain GT-B family-1 UGTs with one glycosyl-transfer activity; soybean Fg3 and the Crocus kaempferol/quercetin sophoroside GT were each characterised as carrying just this activity.
direction_note: Glycosyl transfer from UDP-glucose with UDP release is the only direction a biosynthetic UGT runs in vivo, so ModelSEED's reverse-only assignment inverts the enzyme.

enzyme_name: none identified - non-enzymatic water addition to a caffeate-derived o-benzoquinone
organism_context: plant esculetin-from-caffeate route (AraCyc/BrachyCyc entry); quinone generated upstream by polyphenol oxidase/peroxidase
rationale: This entry isolates hydration of a highly electrophilic o-quinone intermediate; no protein has been reported to catalyse the water addition and no literature on a catalyst for RXN-8333 was located, so the catalysing enzyme is genuinely unknown (and may not exist).
direction_note: Nucleophilic water addition to an o-quinone is fast and effectively irreversible under cellular conditions, so the hydrating left-to-right direction is the real one.

enzyme_name: none identified - spontaneous lactonisation of the cis-ortho-hydroxycinnamate to the coumarin (esculetin)
organism_context: plant coumarin biosynthesis; reconstituted in E. coli with only 4CL + F6'H
rationale: Coumarin ring closure from a cis-ortho-hydroxycinnamate is a spontaneous lactonisation: esculetin, umbelliferone and scopoletin are all produced in E. coli from the corresponding hydroxycinnamates by expressing only 4CL and the F6'H hydroxylase, with no lactone-forming enzyme supplied, so no catalyst is required for this step.
direction_note: Lactonisation with loss of water is thermodynamically downhill and chemically spontaneous, and the coumarin is the metabolic sink, so the left-to-right direction is correct.

enzyme_name: C18->C20 (Delta-6) fatty-acid elongase condensing enzyme (ELOVL/ELO-family 3-ketoacyl-CoA synthase)
organism_context: vertebrate and microalgal n-3 LC-PUFA biosynthesis; ER membrane elongation cycle
rationale: Elongation of stearidonate (18:4 n-3) to eicosatetraenoate (20:4 n-3) is the four-reaction ER elongase cycle; the substrate-selective, rate-setting step is the ELOVL condensing enzyme, a single-activity 3-ketoacyl-CoA synthase, with the reductase/dehydratase/reductase steps carried by three separate proteins (KAR, HACD, TECR) - a pathway of distinct polypeptides, not a fused multifunctional chain.
direction_note: Malonyl-CoA, NADPH and the CoA thioester chemistry are all absent - ModelSEED flags MI:C:2/H:4, exactly the two added carbons - and real elongation is driven irreversibly by malonyl decarboxylation, so left to right is the enzymatic direction.

enzyme_name: no defined enzyme - reduced corrinoid / cytochrome-mediated reductive dechlorination
organism_context: Acetobacterium woodii, Shewanella putrefaciens and other anaerobes; largely fortuitous transition-metal-cofactor chemistry in the carbon tetrachloride degradation route
rationale: Reductive dechlorination steps of the carbon tetrachloride pathway are carried out by reduced corrinoids, cytochromes and other low-potential cofactors rather than by a purified, dedicated dehalogenase; no enzyme catalysing CH3Cl -> CH4 specifically has been characterised.
direction_note: The two-electron donor is missing (ModelSEED flags CI:-2); reductive dechlorination is very strongly exergonic and one-way, and no cell re-chlorinates methane, so ModelSEED's reverse-only direction is wrong.

enzyme_name: allene oxide synthase/hydrolase CYP74C3 (LeAOS3, tomato 9-allene oxide synthase)
distinct_activities: allene oxide hydrolase (alpha-ketol synthase) - the reaction written here
allene oxide cyclase (EC 5.3.99.6), giving rac-cis-10-oxo-11-phytoenoic acid
organism_context: Solanum lycopersicum; CYP74C subfamily. Ordinary CYP74A allene oxide synthases perform only the synthase step, so the polyfunctionality is subfamily-specific.
rationale: Grechkin et al. showed recombinant tomato CYP74C3 not only synthesises the allene oxide 9,10-EOD but also hydrolyses it to the alpha-ketol (this reaction) and cyclises it to 10-oxo-PEA - three distinct catalytic activities on one P450 polypeptide, demonstrated both on in-situ and on preformed 9,10-EOD made by a separate maize CYP74A.
direction_note: The allene oxide is an extremely unstable epoxide that hydrolyses to the alpha-ketol within seconds, enzymatically or spontaneously; there is no reverse reaction, so ModelSEED's reverse-only direction is wrong, and the enzyme's extra hydrolase activity is precisely what commits flux left to right.

enzyme_name: unidentified Trp side-chain-shortening enzyme ('AMI synthase') of gramine biosynthesis
organism_context: Hordeum vulgare (barley)
rationale: Ishikawa et al. (2023) state explicitly that the step preceding 3-aminomethylindole formation - the Trp side-chain shortening - has not been revealed, and their stable-isotope labelling shows it proceeds via a novel intramolecular rearrangement that loses the alpha-carbon; only the two downstream N-methylations have a cloned enzyme.
direction_note: The whole lost C2 fragment is dropped from the equation (ModelSEED flags MI:C:-2/H:-1/O:-2); biosynthetic flux in barley runs Trp -> AMI -> gramine, i.e. left to right.

enzyme_name: purine hydroxylase (PH), a selenium-dependent molybdenum hydroxylase
organism_context: Clostridium purinolyticum (anaerobic purine fermentation); xanthine-dehydrogenase family, distinct from the separate C. purinolyticum XDH
rationale: PH is the Mo/Se/FAD/2Fe-2S hydroxylase of anaerobic purine degradation that installs ring hydroxyls on hypoxanthine using water as oxygen donor and NADP+ as electron acceptor; its reported NADPH-oxidase side reaction is flavin-site chemistry of the same hydroxylase (as in xanthine oxidoreductase), not a second fused catalytic domain, and the cofactor-bearing parts are separate subunits of a complex.
direction_note: The two-electron acceptor NADP+ is missing (ModelSEED flags CI:2); in a purine-fermenting anaerobe the hydroxylation runs one way, toward the more oxidised purine, so left to right is correct.

enzyme_name: purine hydroxylase (PH), a selenium-dependent molybdenum hydroxylase
organism_context: Clostridium purinolyticum (anaerobic purine fermentation, MetaCyc PWY-5497)
rationale: Same enzyme as the hypoxanthine hydroxylation: PH hydroxylates the purine ring at successive positions with water as oxygen donor and NADP+ as acceptor. It is a multi-cofactor, multi-subunit molybdenum hydroxylase - a complex, not a fused bifunctional chain - so the hydroxylase activity is scored monofunctional.
direction_note: Only one H+ and no electron acceptor are written for a 2-electron hydroxylation (ModelSEED flags CI:2); with NADP+ restored the hydroxylation is one-way, left to right.

enzyme_name: flavin-containing S-oxygenating monooxygenase (S-alk(en)yl-L-cysteine S-oxygenase, class-B FMO)
organism_context: Allium sativum AsFMO1 (alliin biosynthesis); a Schizosaccharomyces pombe FMO makes S-methyl-L-cysteine sulfoxide directly. The specific plant enzyme of the methiin pathway (PWY-7614) is not cloned.
rationale: S-oxygenation of S-alk(en)yl-L-cysteines to their sulfoxides is carried out by single-domain, NADPH/O2-dependent class-B flavin monooxygenases - garlic AsFMO1 was identified and structurally characterised, and an S. pombe FMO performs exactly this S-methyl-cysteine oxidation; the plant methiin enzyme itself is unidentified, so the assignment rests on chemistry rather than on this reaction's own protein.
direction_note: The entry substitutes H2O + O2 -> H2O2 for the real NADPH + O2 -> H2O couple; with NADPH restored the sulfoxidation is irreversible left to right, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is wrong.

enzyme_name: none identified
organism_context: Allium sativum (garlic) S-allyl-cysteine / alliin context
rationale: No enzyme is known that condenses L-cysteine with a C3H4 hydrocarbon (ModelSEED maps the partner to 1-cyclopropene, C3H4); the established route to S-allyl-L-cysteine in garlic is glutathione S-conjugation followed by gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase and carboxypeptidase trimming, which this entry does not represent.
direction_note: Neither direction corresponds to a characterised enzyme; the physiological S-allyl-cysteine supply comes from an entirely different glutathione-conjugate route, so the enzymology cannot adjudicate this disagreement.

enzyme_name: GDP-perosamine synthase (Per), a PLP-dependent sugar aminotransferase
organism_context: Caulobacter crescentus (crystal structures), Vibrio cholerae O1 and E. coli O157 O-antigen biosynthesis
rationale: Per is a single-activity homodimeric PLP aminotransferase that transfers the L-glutamate amino group to C4 of GDP-4-keto-6-deoxy-D-mannose; the Cook & Holden structures show one active site running one chemistry, with no second catalytic domain. (ModelSEED's product label '4-amino-4,6-dideoxy-D-mannose' is a misnomer - its formula C16H25N6O14P2 is the GDP-linked sugar.)
direction_note: A transamination consumes no water, and the spurious H2O leaves the entry O-unbalanced (ModelSEED MI:O:-1); pathway flux is biosynthetic, left to right, although PLP transaminases are intrinsically near-equilibrium and the in vivo direction is helped by the glutamate/2-oxoglutarate pool.

enzyme_name: coniine N-methyltransferase (S-adenosyl-L-methionine:coniine methyltransferase)
organism_context: Conium maculatum (poison hemlock)
rationale: The terminal coniine -> N-methylconiine step is a SAM-dependent amine N-methyltransferase, but only in-silico transcript candidates exist - Peddinti et al. state that in vitro testing is still needed to confirm the assignment - so monofunctionality is inferred from the enzyme class rather than demonstrated for this protein.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer is physiologically unidirectional and N-methylconiine accumulates as a pathway end product, so left to right is the enzymatic direction.

enzyme_name: unidentified rotenoid prenyltransferase (DMAPP:9-demethylmunduserone dimethylallyltransferase)
organism_context: rotenoid-producing legumes (Derris, Lonchocarpus, Amorpha) and Mirabilis himalaica
rationale: The step is a DMAPP prenylation of 9-demethylmunduserone established by isotope-feeding work (Crombie & Whiting), but no rotenoid prenyltransferase has been purified or cloned; recent reviews and rotenoid transcriptome/proteome studies still list the prenylation as uncharacterised, so neither the protein nor its functionality can be stated.
direction_note: DMAPP and the released diphosphate are both absent - ModelSEED flags MI:C:5/H:8, exactly the prenyl unit - and prenyl transfer with PPi release is irreversible, so biosynthetic flux runs left to right.

enzyme_name: DHNA dimethylallyltransferase RcDT1 (UbiA-superfamily prenyltransferase) - first pathway-specific step only
organism_context: Rubia cordifolia / R. tinctorum (madder); plastid-localised, root-specific; DHNA-prenylation activity recruited convergently from ubiquinone biosynthesis in Rubiaceae
rationale: RcDT1 is a single-activity UbiA-family membrane prenyltransferase that converts DHNA + DMAPP into 2-carboxyl-3-prenyl-1,4-naphthoquinone, the first alizarin-specific step; the subsequent cyclisation, oxidation and decarboxylation to alizarin are separate and still uncharacterised, so no one enzyme performs the reaction as written.
direction_note: Several enzymatic steps are merged and PPi/CO2 omitted (ModelSEED flags MI:C:-2/H:-9/O:-7/P:-2); every merged step is biosynthetic and the prenyl transfer releases PPi irreversibly, so the direction is left to right.

enzyme_name: methylphloracetophenone synthase (MPAS), a non-reducing iterative type I polyketide synthase
distinct_activities: ketosynthase - decarboxylative Claisen condensation of malonyl units
Claisen-cyclase (CLC) domain - cyclisation and product release
organism_context: Cladonia uncialis mycobiont (lichen); methylphloracetophenone is the monomer that MPAO then dimerises to usnic acid
rationale: Building 2,4,6-trihydroxy-3-methylacetophenone from malonyl-CoA requires a non-reducing PKS carrying KS, AT, ACP, a carbon-methyltransferase (CMeT) and a terminal Claisen-cyclase domain on one polypeptide - genuinely distinct chemistries fused in a single chain; the gene (mpas) was identified by genome mining and shown transcriptionally active, but not yet reconstituted in vitro.
direction_note: The entry is grossly unbalanced - the entire CoA moiety, the additional malonyl units and SAM are all missing (ModelSEED MI:C:-15/H:-23/N:-7/O:-15/P:-3/S:-1) - but polyketide chain assembly is driven irreversibly by malonyl decarboxylation, so the biosynthetic left-to-right sense is the right one.

enzyme_name: unidentified C7-cyclitol (valienone) reductase of the validamycin val gene cluster
organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus var. limoneus and subsp. jinggangensis 5008 (validamycin A biosynthesis)
rationale: Isotope-labelled intermediate feeding and 45-kb cluster annotation place a valienone-to-validone reduction in the validamycin pathway, but no val gene product has been biochemically assigned to it; the enzymes actually characterised are ValA (C7-cyclitol synthase), ValC (C7-cyclitol kinase), ValL (validoxylamine A 7'-phosphate synthase), VldE and ValG.
direction_note: The NAD(P)H donor is replaced by two bare protons (ModelSEED flags CI:-2); the pathway runs valienone -> validone -> validamine, so the reductive left-to-right direction is the enzymatic one.

enzyme_name: unidentified C7-cyclitol (valienone 7-phosphate) reductase of the validamycin val gene cluster
organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus subsp. jinggangensis 5008; the 7-phosphorylated cyclitols (made by the ValC kinase) are the on-pathway intermediates
rationale: This is the phosphorylated, on-pathway counterpart of the valienone reduction: ValC phosphorylates C7 of the cyclitol, after which valienone 7-phosphate is reduced to validone 7-phosphate en route to validamine 7-phosphate, but no cluster gene has been biochemically assigned to the reductase step.
direction_note: The NAD(P)H donor is replaced by two bare protons (ModelSEED flags CI:-2); biosynthesis proceeds valienone 7-P -> validone 7-P -> validamine 7-P, so left to right is the enzymatic direction.
